2.text: In the Kolyma district, on the western side of the mountains, the climate is

3.text: cold and dry. The snowfall is not so heavy, and tempests are not so frequent,

4.text: in the coldest time of the year, as on the Chukchee Peninsula.

5.text: On the Pacific coast, while the temperature does not fall so low, the

6.text: snowfall is much heavier; and snow-tempests, dry in winter, and damp and

7.text: misty in the fall and spring, often last for several weeks without cessation.

8.text: Therefore the floras of the two districts are quite different. On the Kolyma

9.text: side the chief tree is the larch, which attains a great height and has a well-

10.text: developed form even beyond the polar circle and as far north as latitude 69°.

11.text: The limit of its distribution is quite sharp, and runs along the larger rivers,

12.text: about fifty miles from the seacoast. Shrubby willows of about a man’s height,

13.text: are found even twenty miles farther north, and their growth becomes stunted

14.text: only a few miles from the seacoast. On the Pacific side — in the valley,

15.text: of the Anadyr River, for example — the larch-tree is less commonly found

16.text: than west of the mountains, and thrives only in the interior portion of the

17.text: country, along the river Main, a tributary of the Anadyr. The chief trees are

18.text: the willow and the poplar, which are distributed about evenly. Even on the

19.text: southern side of the polar circle, a hundred miles from the coast, their growth

20.text: becomes stunted, but as shrubs they continue for some distance to the north.

21.text: Almost everywhere some very small shrubby willows and alders are found in

22.text: the river-valleys. The coast for many miles is bare of every kind of growth

23.text: except reindeer-moss and a few lichens. On sandy spots, like Indian Point,

24.text: the inhabitants cannot gather grass enough even for the soles of their boots,

25.text: and are obliged to bring it from farther inland.

26.text: Bogdanovitch mentions that he has seen good grass on the mountain-slopes

27.text: around Konyam Bay, but he does not specify how large these grassy spots

28.text: were; he even expresses the opinion that the Chukchee Peninsula can be

29.text: crossed with horses in the summer-time.¹ I wish to point out, however, that

30.text: even farther to the south, along the forest-line, horses used for travelling²

31.text: often starve for want of fodder.
